why: I checked every verifier PASS/FAIL condition against its expect line. None is stricter than its line. Check 1 asks only for the `<file>:<line>: ` prefix followed by some error text, not exact wording. Check 2 asks for exit 2 and any non-empty stderr. Check 3 checks `line` and `error`. Check 4 checks the fields the line names and "no non-empty `dependencies`". Checks 5 and 6 follow their lines. The stricter extras (CRLF, shebang, executable mode, stdout-only output, lockfile) appear only under "Advisory (not pass/fail)" or in builder steps. Nothing sets branch-name rules, mutation tests or file-touch limits. Every behaviour line is checked by running the program: the CLI on temp fixtures, `lint` imported and called, `npm test`, and `npm ci && npm test` at the head. File reads are used only where the line is about files (package.json, README, test files).
